source.title: Caring babies: Concern for others in distress during infancy

confidence_rationale: Strong longitudinal design (N=165 followed 3->18 months) directly measuring the two streams Q-073 cares about: registration of others' distress vs prosocial action on others' behalf. Finds the distress-registration stream online and consistent by ~3 months and plateauing in year two, while prosocial (appetitive, other-benefiting) action surges later in year two -- a genuine ordering asymmetry. Confidence held below 0.8 because the paper measures empathic concern for distress, not REE's full 'other-bound suffering/threat' stream, and 'prosocial action' is a behavioural composite that is not identical to REE's 'other-bound liking/wanting'.
failure_signatures: Concern for distressed others did not climb steeply with age -- it appeared early and plateaued in the second year -- so a model that expects other-bound suffering to RAMP UP in parallel with appetitive prosociality is contradicted; the suffering channel saturates early while the appetitive channel is still rising.

The paper refutes discrete stage theories of empathy; an ordering enforced as a hard developmental gate (suffering stage fully completes, THEN liking stage opens) is not supported -- both streams overlap and develop gradually.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Observable concern for others in distress is present and individually consistent from as early as 3 months of age and grows only modestly thereafter, plateauing in the second year; in contrast, prosocial behaviour on behalf of distressed others increases rapidly during the second year, and early individual differences in concern predict later prosocial behaviour.
mapping.ree_translation: Maps onto Q-073's ordering question: the other-bound SUFFERING-registration stream (concern for others' distress) comes online developmentally earlier and stabilises before the other-bound APPETITIVE / action stream (prosocial helping that confers benefit on others) reaches full strength. This is consistent with REE's 'protection-first' framing (MECH-408 developmental ordering on the ARC-059 social spine) -- register harm-to-others before instantiating benefit-to-others -- and the predictive link (early concern -> later prosociality) is consistent with the suffering stream acting as a developmental scaffold for the appetitive stream rather than the reverse.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Empathic concern for distress is a proxy for REE's 'other-bound suffering/threat' stream, not an identity: concern is an affective-resonance measure, whereas REE's stream is about valuing harm-to-others in an action-selection sense. Likewise 'prosocial behaviour' bundles helping/comforting/sharing and is not the same construct as REE's 'other-bound liking/wanting' (which is closer to vicarious reward / wanting good things FOR another). The paper says nothing about the EXPLOITATION-VULNERABILITY hypothesis (that early positive other-reward would be gameable) -- it speaks only to which stream matures first, not to WHY the ordering is adaptive.
mapping.source_context: Longitudinal observational study, N=165 Israeli infants, assessed at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months; coded responses to staged distress of others (experimenter/parent) and prosocial behaviour.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (large longitudinal sample, repeated measures, predictive validity, published in a strong developmental journal). Mapping fidelity is the limiting factor: the constructs are adjacent to but not identical with REE's other-bound streams, and human infant ontogeny is being read as a prior on an artificial agent's stream-ordering. Transfer risk moderate-to-elevated because REE is not a developing human and the 'why' of the ordering (protection vs exploitation-resistance) is not addressed by this paper.
